title: Prompt Sets & Benchmarks: Onboarding and Triage Playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview:
This playbook describes the standard process for onboarding new prompt sets and benchmark suites into Redwood's eval ecosystem, and the triage workflow to follow when benchmarks regress. Intended audience: applied ML engineers, evaluation owners, model-onboarding engineers, and SREs who monitor production regressions.

Goals:
- Provide a reproducible, low-friction onboarding path for new prompt sets and benchmark tasks.
- Standardize metric definitions and thresholds used for release decisions.
- Define a deterministic triage & escalation loop for quality regressions tied to model rollouts, quantization changes, or runtime/serving changes.

Scope:
- This document covers: prompt set naming conventions, dataset requirements, benchmark configuration, baseline metrics and thresholds, automated evaluation CI/CD, regression triage steps, and ownership/escalation.
- Not covered: low-level data labeling standards (see related data-management docs) or experiment design for research-only benchmarks.

Ownership and contacts:
- Owner: Applied ML & Evals team (applied-ml@redwood.com)
- Primary contact for onboarding questions: Maya Patel (maya@redwood.com)
body_2:
Owners for stages:
- Prompt set curator (team that owns the product integration) — responsible for dataset validity and business acceptance criteria.
- Eval owner (applied-ml) — responsible for CI integration, metric definitions, and baseline generation.
- Oncall (SRE) — responsible for monitoring alerts tied to deployed model regressions.

Onboarding checklist (ordered steps):
1) Draft prompt set and metadata
   - Provide: name, short description, task type (classification/generation/ranking), language(s), target distribution (sample rates, domains), and a reference acceptance test.
   - Naming convention: {team}-{task}-{short-slug}-{v#} e.g., billing-invoice-summarization-v1
2) Validate dataset requirements
   - Minimum examples: 500 for classification, 200 for ranking, 100 for open-ended generation (recommended).
   - Format: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson). Each record must include: id, input, expected_output (if available), labels (if applicable), metadata.tags (list).
   - Data quality checks: no PII, minimum token length checks, example-level pass-fail annotation coverage >= 10% for initial onboarding.
3) Create benchmark config
   - Provide model-compatible prompt templates and scoring function. Attach quantization recommendations (if known).
   - Example config fields: task_type, prompt_template, scoring: exact_match|f1|rouge-l|custom_script, evaluation_batch_size.
4) Baseline generation and CI integration
   - Eval owner generates baseline results on the current production model and at least two historical model checkpoints.
   - Add benchmark to eval harness CI with a daily scheduled run and on PRs that touch model-serving, quantization profiles, or prompt templates.
5) Stakeholder review and publish
   - Reviewers: product owner + applied-ml eval owner + privacy reviewer (if dataset contains user-derived content). Document signoff in the benchmark metadata.
body_3:
Dataset requirements (summary table):
- Minimum examples: [classification: 500, ranking: 200, generation: 100]
- Format: ndjson with fields: id, input, expected_output, labels, metadata.tags
- Label coverage required: >= 10% initial, target >= 60% after two iterations
- No PII: automatic scanner must return zero PII flags before onboarding.

Metric definitions and thresholds:
- Classification: accuracy and macro-F1. Threshold for regression alert: drop >= 2% absolute accuracy or >= 3 F1 points compared to baseline.
- Ranking: NDCG@10 and MRR. Regression alert: absolute drop of >= 0.03 NDCG or >= 0.04 MRR.
- Generation: BLEU / ROUGE / BERTScore and human preference (if available). Regression alert: > 4 point drop in BERTScore or > 6 point drop in ROUGE-L.
- Critical tasks (high-business-impact): set tighter thresholds in benchmark metadata (defaults are above but can be tightened).
body_4:
Automated evaluation and CI:
- CI policies: every benchmark must be added to the eval-harness YAML and be runnable with the eval CLI.
- Scheduled runs: nightly baseline runs against the current production model and the canary model (if canary exists).
- PR gating: any PR that changes model weights, quantization profiles, or serving runtimes must run affected benchmarks and cannot be merged if a regression is detected on any critical task.

Example eval CLI usage:
- Run a single benchmark locally:
  ./eval-harness run --config benchmarks/billing-invoice-summarization-v1.yaml --model redwood-prod-v3 --out results/summary.json
- Run against a quantized artifact:
  ./eval-harness run --config benchmarks/billing-invoice-summarization-v1.yaml --model redwood-prod-v3-8bit --batch-size 8

Prompt set schema (example ndjson record):
{
  "id": "inv-0001",
  "input": "Summarize the invoice text below into a 3-line summary.",
  "expected_output": "Payment for AWS services due 2027-03-15, amount $1,234.56, invoice #A123.",
  "labels": ["invoice","finance"],
  "metadata.tags": ["onboarding","billing"],
  "metadata.source": "prod-customer-exports"
}

Scoring & custom scripts:
- Where standard metrics are insufficient, attach a custom scoring script (python) under eval-scripts/. Scripts must implement the eval interface: score(predictions, references) -> dict. Include unit tests.
body_5:
Regression triage workflow (step-by-step):
1) Alerting: SRE or applied-ml receives regression alert from eval platform (via PagerDuty channel: PD-EVALS). Attach run id and diff.
2) Initial assessment (15 min): owner inspects diff in CI artifact, checks for common causes: model version change, quantization profile update, runtime change, or serving config.
3) Reproduce locally (30-60 min): rerun the failing benchmark with identical model artifact and flags. Record logs: seed, batch-size, tokenization settings.
4) Scope determination (60 min): determine whether regression is global (all tasks/models), task-specific, or data-related.
5) Mitigation options (choose one):
   - Rollback to previous stable model (If regression severity >= critical threshold).
   - Apply targeted prompt-template patch (if error introduced by prompt change).
   - Increase canary traffic to gather more real-world signals (if unsure).
   - Patch quantization profile or revert quantization commit (if quantization-only regression).
6) Post-mortem and action items: open an incident ticket, assign owners, and add remediation steps. Attach updated baseline results and proposed next steps.

Triage decision matrix (summary):
- Severity: Critical | High | Medium | Low
- Critical: any regression on critical task with > 2% absolute metric drop or user-facing errors in production — escalate to oncall + product + engineering director immediately.
- High: regression that affects important product flows (not immediately customer-facing) — applied-ml + model-serving within 24 hours.
- Medium/Low: schedule fix in next sprint.
body_6:
Observability and SLOs for benchmarks:
- Alerting SLO: detection-to-notification <= 15 minutes for nightly runs.
- Repro time SLO: able to reproduce failing run locally within 60 minutes.
- Regression review SLA: initial triage completed within 4 hours for Critical/High.
- Monitoring: daily trend dashboards for key metrics (accuracy/F1/NDCG/BERTScore) and per-prompt-set time-series. Include token-level latency and cost deltas per benchmark run.

Quantization profile guidance:
- If a benchmark fails after quantization, confirm the exact profile used (per-model quantization metadata must be attached to eval run).
- Recommended quantization CI step: run benchmarks on both fp16 and quantized artifacts before approving profile changes.
- Known safe profiles: 8-bit compressed with per-channel symmetric quantization for transformer attention and MLP kernels. Document exceptions in benchmark metadata.
body_7:
Release & rollout guidance:
- Canary: add benchmark to canary CI and track both absolute metric and delta to production baseline.
- Gate: do not promote models to production if any critical benchmark regresses beyond thresholds.
- Rollback criteria: automatic rollback if canary observes a regression meeting critical criteria on 3 consecutive runs.

Escalation matrix:
- PD-EVALS (pagerduty): Applied-ML oncall (primary), Eng-SRE oncall (secondary)
- Email escalation: applied-ml@redwood.com, model-serving@redwood.com, product-owner@redwood.com

Runbook snippets and debugging checklist:
- Commands:
  - ./eval-harness run --config <config> --model <model> --save-logs
  - ./eval-harness compare --baseline results/baseline.json --current results/current.json
- Debug checklist:
  1) Confirm identical tokenization and model artifact sha256.
  2) Check quantization metadata in eval run metadata JSON.
  3) Verify sample-level diffs and failure examples.
  4) Check for data drift: run small data-stability checks against recent production samples.
body_8:
Post-incident: documentation and prevention:
- Every regression incident must result in a short postmortem that includes: root cause, action items, who implemented the fix, and validation evidence.
- Preventative measures: expand unit tests for prompt templates, add more labeled examples for brittle tasks, strengthen quantization test coverage.

Appendix: example benchmark config (YAML):
---
name: billing-invoice-summarization-v1
task_type: generation
prompt_template: |
  {{instruction}}
  Invoice text:
  {{input}}
scoring: rouge-l
evaluation_batch_size: 16
quantization_recommendation: 8bit-per-channel
owner: team-billing
criticality: high
---

Appendix: quick links and references:
- Eval harness standards: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Quality guardrails & regression triage: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails/applied-ml-quality-guardrails-and-regression-triage-playbook-2027
- Quantization best practices: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026

If you have questions about onboarding or want a hands-on review, file a ticket in the applied-ml Jira queue (EVALS) and tag @maya.
